subject.title: refactor: separate external conversations from local sessions

question: Should OpenClaw adopt these conversation tools, Gateway methods, plugin-facing contracts, and v11 durable data model as the permanent core API after the cancellation defect and live-proof gate are resolved?
rationale: The branch creates new public protocol and plugin surfaces plus a persisted migration whose long-term ownership and compatibility cannot be decided from automated correctness checks alone.

options.title: Approve after gates
options.body: Adopt the architecture after cancellation is fixed and real Reef plus v10-upgrade proof demonstrates the full lifecycle.

options.title: Narrow the core contract
options.body: Keep only the generic conversation registry and delivery seam while moving Reef-specific or higher-level turn behavior behind the plugin boundary.

options.title: Pause the refactor
options.body: Do not establish the new API or schema until a smaller design proves the central Reef problem can be solved with existing message and session surfaces.

recommendation.title: Approve after gates
recommendation.body: Adopt the architecture after cancellation is fixed and real Reef plus v10-upgrade proof demonstrates the full lifecycle.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the best available routing candidate from the linked feature and prior Gateway/session history, while final approval should remain explicit rather than inferred from authorship.
